concepts.def: The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.
A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.
A smaller cell with no nucleus; DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm; e.g. bacteria.
Parts inside a cell with specific jobs: nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, chloroplasts.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.
Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Organisation of the Organism — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Organisation of the Organism brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Organisation of the Organism.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a prokaryote?
options: Human skin cell
Yeast
Bacterium
Onion cell
protein synthesis
photosynthesis
aerobic respiration
cell division

mcqs.q: What does insulin do to blood glucose?
options: It lowers blood glucose by causing cells (especially liver and muscle) to take it up and store it as glycogen.
Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.
Insulin raises blood glucose to give the body energy.
Both introns and exons are removed and the cell uses just the cap and tail.

mcqs.q: After pre-mRNA splicing in eukaryotes, which sequences remain in the mature mRNA?
options: Both introns and exons are removed and the cell uses just the cap and tail.
Introns remain because they encode the protein; exons are removed as junk.
Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.
Exons remain; introns are removed.

mcqs.q: What is produced in anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells?
options: Anaerobic respiration produces ethanol and CO2 in humans.
Lactic acid (lactate) and a small amount of ATP — no CO2 or water in this pathway.
Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.
Anaerobic respiration produces oxygen as a waste product.

mcqs.q: A bacterium is 2 µm long. How many fit end-to-end across a 1 mm gap?
options: 400 bacteria
500 bacteria
750 bacteria
250 bacteria

mcqs.q: Which list shows levels of organisation in the correct order from simplest to most complex?
options: Cell → tissue → organ → organ system
Organ → tissue → cell → organ system
Tissue → cell → organ → organ system
Organ system → organ → cell → tissue

mcqs.q: The stomach contains muscle tissue, glandular tissue and epithelial tissue working together. This makes the stomach an example of a:
options: Organ
Single tissue
Organ system
Single cell

mcqs.q: A red blood cell has no nucleus and is packed with haemoglobin. This is an example of:
options: A specialised cell adapted to its function
An unspecialised stem cell
A prokaryotic cell
A plant cell

mcqs.q: Which of these is an organ system rather than an organ?
options: The digestive system
The heart
The liver
The stomach
